units.title: Stephen Hawking
units.blurb: Reading guides to A Brief History of Time (1988) and The Universe in a Nutshell (2001).

units.title: Carl Sagan
units.blurb: Reading guides to Cosmos (1980) and Sagan's other books.

topics.title: Hawking: A Brief History of Time
topics.short: A chapter-by-chapter guide, in our own words, to Stephen Hawking's 1988 book about space, time, black holes and the beginning of the universe.
topics.trouble: Readers think black holes suck in everything nearby; far from one, its gravity is the same as any object of the same mass.

topics.title: Hawking: The Universe in a Nutshell
topics.short: A guide to Hawking's 2001 follow-up: relativity, the shape of time, predicting the future and whether time travel is possible.
topics.trouble: Readers treat ideas Hawking calls speculative, such as branes, as settled science.

topics.title: Sagan: Cosmos
topics.short: A guide to the 13 chapters of Carl Sagan's 1980 book, written with the television series: the history of science and our place among the stars.
topics.trouble: Readers think the Cosmic Calendar means the universe is one year old; it squeezes about 13.8 billion years into one year to show how recent people are.

topics.title: Sagan's Other Books
topics.short: Pale Blue Dot, The Demon-Haunted World, The Dragons of Eden, Contact and more: what each is about and how Sagan taught people to test claims.
topics.trouble: Readers think skepticism means doubting everything; Sagan meant asking for evidence and staying open to it.
